blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At rise level, making digital tools productive is mostly about reducing friction. Every extra click, every duplicated workflow, every notification nobody acts on is a small tax on the team's attention. Over a week, those small taxes add up to hours of wasted energy.

The useful habits are boring. Turn off notifications that do not lead to action. Keep shared folders clean so people find what they need in seconds. Agree as a team how meetings end — decisions, actions, owners — so that the tool simply records what was decided. Write short messages. Read before replying.

Good tools used well feel quiet. You know what is expected of you, you find what you need quickly, and you leave at the end of the day with your inbox roughly under control. That quietness is the real product of rise-level digital hygiene — and the absence of it is what makes modern work feel so exhausting.

items.q: According to the text, making digital tools productive is mostly about…
items.why: "making digital tools productive is mostly about reducing friction."

items.q: How does the text describe the useful habits?
items.why: "The useful habits are boring." — o valor está na disciplina, não na novidade.

items.q: What should a tool do once a team agrees how meetings end?
items.why: "so that the tool simply records what was decided."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Small inefficiencies add up over time.
Clean shared folders save people time.
More notifications generally mean a more productive team.
items.why: Inferência: o texto trata notificações inúteis como uma 'taxa' sobre a atenção — mais delas não é sinal de produtividade.

items.q: The phrase "That quietness is the real product" suggests that…
options: productivity software should be sold as a product
the goal is calm, low-friction work, not the tool itself
items.why: Inferência: o 'produto' desejado é o estado de trabalho tranquilo e sem atrito que boas práticas produzem.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily conduzindo o workshop. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, thanks for giving me twenty minutes. This isn't a training session, and I'm not going to teach you any new software. We're just going to fix a few small, boring things — and by Friday most of you will have got about two hours back.

Let's start with your phones. Open your notification settings right now. Anything that isn't a real person waiting on a real answer — turn it off. Marketing emails, app badges, the little red dots. If it doesn't lead to an action, it's just noise pulling at your attention all day.

Next, the shared drive. We currently have four folders all called 'Final'. That's not a folder problem, that's a habit problem. So from today, one place for each project, clear names, and we delete the duplicates as we go.

Last thing, and this is the big one. Every meeting ends the same way: decisions, actions, owners. Thirty seconds. Someone types it into the notes while we're still in the room. No more 'who was doing that again?' emails on Monday.

None of this is clever. That's exactly the point. Do the boring things well, and the tools finally get quiet.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily say the workshop is NOT?
options: A training session teaching new software
items.why: "This isn't a training session, and I'm not going to teach you any new software."

items.q: Which notifications does Emily tell the team to turn off?
options: Anything that isn't a real person waiting on a real answer
items.why: "Anything that isn't a real person waiting on a real answer — turn it off."

items.q: Why does Emily mention the four folders all called 'Final'?
options: To show the drive is running out of space
As an example of a habit problem, not a folder problem
To praise how the team names files
items.why: "That's not a folder problem, that's a habit problem."

items.q: What does Emily mean when she says "Do the boring things well, and the tools finally get quiet"?
options: The team should mute all devices during work
People should stop using shared drives
Simple, consistent habits remove the noise and distraction
items.why: Inferência: 'quiet' aqui é a ausência de atrito e ruído que boas rotinas produzem — não silêncio literal.

items.q: What is Emily's attitude toward her own advice?
options: She thinks it is clever and original
She admits it is unglamorous, and treats that as the point
She is unsure whether it will work
She apologises for how difficult it is
items.why: Inferência: "None of this is clever. That's exactly the point." — ela valoriza justamente o caráter simples.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every extra login step adds friction to the process." Here, friction means…
items.why: Friction = atrito: aquilo que torna o fluxo mais lento e trabalhoso.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Two teams were entering the same data twice — a classic ___ that wasted everyone's time."
items.why: Duplicated workflow = fluxo duplicado: o mesmo trabalho feito duas vezes.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Those five-minute delays don't seem like much, but they ___ to hours by the end of the week."
items.why: To add up = somar-se, acumular até virar um total significativo.

items.q: Digital hygiene is best described as…
options: the routines that keep tools tidy and low-friction
items.why: Digital hygiene = higiene digital: os hábitos que mantêm ferramentas e fluxos organizados e leves.

items.q: "By 6 p.m. she had her inbox roughly under control." An inbox is…
options: the place where incoming messages arrive
items.why: Inbox = caixa de entrada: onde chegam as mensagens recebidas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre produtividade e ferramentas. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's turn off the notifications that don't lead to action." To turn off means to…
items.why: Turn off = desligar, desativar.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new folder system across all teams next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "A couple of managers pushed back on muting all app badges." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo proposto.

items.q: "Everyone liked the idea, but nobody followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Cleaning up the shared drive really moved the needle on how fast people found files." This means it…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
